MIND. [1] [Chlor.]
Quiet delirium in alternation with the greatest restlessness and desire to run away. θ Typhus.
Intoxicated feeling with sopor and great nervous irritation ; dry mouth and diarrhœa. θ Typhus.
After excitement. θ Spasmus glottidis.
   

SENSORIUM. [2] [Chlor.]
Disposition to faint. θ Typhus.
Coma, fainting and cold, viscous sweats. θ Typhus. θ Scarlatina. θ Measles. θ Variola.
Partially comatose during suffocative attack.
   

SIGHT AND EYES. [5] [Chlor.]
Dull and glassy expression of eyes. θ Spasmus glottidis.
Staring eyes.
Running of tears < in open air.
Purulent ophthalmia.
   

HEARING AND EARS. [6] [Chlor.]
Deafness. θ Typhus.
   

SMELL AND NOSE. [7] [Chlor.]
Nose smoky or sooty. θ Typhus.
Coryza with headache.
   

UPPER FACE. [8] [Chlor.]
Face pale and bloated. θ Spasmus glottidis.
Child became livid. θ Spasm of glottis.
Face extremely livid, blue.
Ash-colored face. θ Typhus.
   

LOWER FACE. [9] [Chlor.]
Lips, tongue and teeth brown, black and sooty. θ Typhus.
   

TEETH AND GUMS. [10] [Chlor.]
Teeth black.
   

TASTE, SPEECH, TONGUE. [11] [Chlor.]
Tongue dry. θ Typhus.
Tongue black.
   

INNER MOUTH. [12] [Chlor.]
Dryness of whole buccal cavity. θ Typhus.
Putrid odor from mouth. θ Stomacace.
   

APPETITE, THIRST. DESIRES, AVERSIONS. [14] [Chlor.]
Loss of appetite. θ Spasmus glottidis.
   

STOOLS AND RECTUM. [20] [Chlor.]
Diarrhœa with dryness of mouth, after the appearance of eruption in typhus.
Hemorrhage from bowels in typhus ; blood black, coagulated or thin, smelling like carrion.
Diarrhœa in the morning.
   

VOICE AND LARYNX. TRACHEA AND BRONCHIA. [25] [Chlor.]
Aphonia from damp air.
Spasms of vocal cords.
Sensation of constriction in air tubes, tightness and suffocation.
Violent irritation in epiglottis, larynx, and bronchial tubes.
Violent spasms of glottis ; air is admitted well enough, but its exit is prevented.
Thirty or forty attacks of spasmus glottidis occurring within twenty-four hours.
   

RESPIRATION. [26] [Chlor.]
Sudden tightness of chest.
Sudden and extreme dyspnœa from spasm of vocal cords.
Dyspnœa increasing, great anxiety, not that he thinks he will die, but on account of the impeded respiration ; physical, not psychical anxiety.
Paroxysms of suffocation followed by catarrh.
Inspiration easy, but could not completely fill the lungs with air.
Inspiration is attended by a short crackling rale.
Suddenly and without warning, child makes a long crowing inspiration, an attempt is made to exhale, but without success ; another crowing inspiration followed by a forcible, but ineffectual effort to exhale ; and this was repeated until she became blue around the mouth ; and sank into partial unconsciousness, when free inspiration would take place and child would generally sink into deep sleep ; frequently towards close of an attack, convulsive movements of extremities take place. θ Spasmus glottidis.
Inspiration unimpeded and can be effected in the natural manner, but expiration is absolutely impossible.
Gasping inhalation and expiration nearly impossible.
Breathing consists of a succession of crowing inspirations, each followed by an ineffectual effort at expiration, inflating the chest to a more painful extent. θ Spasmus glottidis. θ Emphysema pulmonum.
Crowing inspiration ; absolutely obstructed expiration ; face turgid and livid ; convulsive movements of extremities ; partial coma.
Expiration difficult, prolonged, and seems as if insufficient, as if air cells were hardly half empty.
   

COUGH. [27] [Chlor.]
Any attempt to cough produces spasm of glottis.
Desire to cough resulting from a tickling and a sensation of rawness behind the thyroid cartilage ; when he seeks to yield to this desire he finds it impossible to expel the air from the chest ; the cough is therefore abortive, although the desire grows continually more and more intense ; the obstruction to cough results from an apparent constriction just below larynx, although he can draw air freely into the lungs.
The freedom of inhalation and impeded exhalation, together with constantly increasing tickling in larynx which compelled him to make very energetic but unavailing efforts to cough, continue until he sinks exhausted and covered with sweat upon a couch, when spasm seems to relax and he can cough and exhale with comparative freedom ; paroxysms recur about every two hours. θ Spasmodic cough.
A continuous little dry cough.
Cough, with spitting of blood, with pleuritic pains.
   

INNER CHEST AND LUNGS. [28] [Chlor.]
Inflammation of lungs and air passages. θ Phthisis pulmonalis.
   

HEART, PULSE AND CIRCULATION. [29] [Chlor.]
Pulse small and soft.
Congestion to head and chest.
   

LIMBS IN GENERAL. [34] [Chlor.]
Convulsive movements of extremities.
   

REST. POSITION. MOTION. [35] [Chlor.]
Inclination to lie down with pain in head and exhaustion.
   

NERVES. [36] [Chlor.]
Loss of strength and playfulness. θ Spasmus glottidis.
Great prostration. θ Typhus.
The nervous symptoms continually increase in third or fourth week of typhus.
Subsultus tendinum. θ Typhus.
Violent spasms with the coming of eye teeth.
The interrupted breathing results in asphyxia with or without convulsions, during which relaxation follows and free perspiration takes place again. θ Laryngismus stridulus.
Towards close of an attack convulsive movements. θ Laryngismus stridulus.
   

SLEEP. [37] [Chlor.]
Attacks of spasmus glottidis occur frequently during sleep, arousing child suddenly ; they are most frequent from midnight to 7 A. M.
   

TIME. [38] [Chlor.]
Wakens at 3 or 4 A. M. with apprehension of a terrible disease coming on.
Acts quicker when taken in evening.
   

FEVER. [40] [Chlor.]
Burning dry heat with anxiety and raving. θ Typhus.
Cold sweat covers body.
A genial glow all over surface with night sweat during sleep.
Night sweat of consumptives.
In typhus give five drops of chlorine water every two or three hours until tongue gets moist (Goullon, Sr.).
   

TISSUES. [44] [Chlor.]
Rapid emaciation. θ Spasmus glottidis.
Loss of fat ; absorption of fat.
Acute rheumatic pains.
   

SKIN. [46] [Chlor.]
Excessive sensitiveness of skin.
Cutis anserina ; dry, yellow and shrivelled.
Typhoid state in scarlatina, measles, variola, spotted and putrid fever. θ Typhus.
